improvements.name: CamemBERT L2 with Focal Loss + Label Smoothing
improvements.actual_result: Standalone acc=0.8100 / f1m=0.6087 (weaker accuracy). In the hybrid with XGB v2 it lifts f1m from 0.6608 to 0.6722.
improvements.rationale: F1-macro (57.3%) lags far behind accuracy (82.0%) — the model is bad at rare classes. Focal loss down-weights easy/frequent samples and forces the model to learn rare patterns.

improvements.name: XGBoost with L2 CamemBERT Embeddings
improvements.actual_result: Hybrid (run2 + XGB v2, max_conf): acc=0.8467 / f1m=0.6608 / f1w=0.8440 — beats baseline on all metrics. Biggest single win.
improvements.rationale: Current XGBoost uses L1 encoder embeddings (optimized for 157-class task). L2 embeddings have learned finer subcategory distinctions. Concatenating both gives complementary signal.

improvements.name: Meta-Learner Stacking

parameters.decision_target: 1=use XGBoost (when it's right and CamemBERT is wrong)

improvements.rationale: max_conf is a global rule. A meta-learner can learn per-context patterns (e.g., 'trust XGBoost more when confidence gap is large AND models disagree').

improvements.name: XGBoost v3 — concat embeddings + engineered text features
improvements.expected_improvement: small accuracy/F1 gain from explicit non-linear text signals
improvements.actual_result: Hybrid (focal + XGB v3, max_conf): acc=0.8479 / f1m=0.6728 / f1w=0.8467 — only +0.06pp f1m over v2. Engineered features add almost nothing; the embeddings already capture them.
improvements.time_estimate: ~2h (reuses cached v2 concat embeddings, no GPU for features)
improvements.rationale: Trees benefit from explicit signals (lengths, digit/upper/punct ratios) that are hard to read off a CLS embedding. Strict superset of v2 features.

improvements.name: XGBoost v3_balanced — v3 features + inverse-frequency class weighting (rare-class booster)
improvements.expected_improvement: F1-macro gain on the long tail (trees' analogue of focal loss)
improvements.actual_result: Hybrid (focal + XGB v3_balanced, max_conf): acc=0.8490 / f1m=0.6814 / f1w=0.8480 — NEW STANDARD. +0.92pp f1m over focal+v2. The rare-class weighting is the real win.

parameters.weight_formula: w_subcat = (N / n_subcat) ** alpha, normalized to mean 1, capped at BALANCE_CAP

improvements.rationale: Inverse-frequency sample weights amplify rare L2 subcategories the same way focal loss does for the CamemBERT branch — directly targets F1-macro. Engineered features alone (v3) did nothing; the weighting added +0.9pp f1m.

improvements.name: kNN / Nearest-Class-Mean tail expert — third voter for the long tail
improvements.output_dir: (no model file — NCM centroids rebuilt from cached embeddings at eval time)
improvements.expected_improvement: F1-macro on the ultra-rare + rare bands, accuracy-neutral
improvements.actual_result: Adopted at margin tau=0.15: acc=0.8487 / f1m=0.6912 — +0.98pp f1m for -0.03pp acc. ~+1pp f1m, well below the +15.8pp oracle ceiling (limited by detector precision/recall tradeoff).
improvements.time_estimate: ~15-25 min CPU (reuses cached concat embeddings, no GPU, no training)

parameters.method: Nearest-Class-Mean over ALL 6067 classes (L2-normalized centroids from train concat embeddings, L2-half = run2 768d)
parameters.tail_definition: train count < 100 (2106 classes, ~12.3k val / test samples = ~1% of data)
parameters.gate: margin = sim(nearest tail centroid) - sim(nearest non-tail centroid); override base when margin > tau
parameters.why_margin: absolute cosine-sim has no precision (BERT embeddings anisotropic — everything is moderately similar); margin vs non-tail centroids removes the global-similarity baseline

improvements.rationale: Diagnostic (diagnose_tail.py) found +15.8pp oracle F1-macro headroom in the tail at flat accuracy, with 77-99% of tail errors being 'both base experts wrong' (need a NEW model). A flat NCM tail expert bypasses L1 routing (only the XGBoost branch is L1-capped) and works at 1-5 samples/class where gradient models can't.

execution_order: Step 3 (meta-learner) can run IMMEDIATELY — only needs predictions_cache.pkl
Step 2 (XGBoost v2) needs GPU for embedding extraction (~3h) then CPU for XGBoost
Step 1 (focal loss) is longest (~12-18h) but gives biggest F1-macro gain
After Step 1 completes: re-run threshold sweep with new CamemBERT checkpoint
After Step 2 completes: re-run threshold sweep with new XGBoost
Final: combine all 3 improvements in one sweep

baseline_to_beat.system: max_conf hybrid (CamemBERT L2 run2 + XGBoost v1)

final_result.system: Focal L2 + XGBoost v3_balanced (max_conf) + kNN/NCM tail expert (margin tau=0.15)
final_result.config: max_conf base (XGB on ~41% of contested) + tail override where NCM margin > 0.15 (~6k samples)

focal_xgb_v3_balanced.note: rare-class weighting drives the F1-macro gain

plus_knn_tail_expert.note: NEW STANDARD — NCM tail voter, +1pp f1m at ~flat accuracy

decision_layer_study.note: calibration & learned gate both hurt; max_conf confirmed near-optimal — bottleneck is the component models, not the decision rule
